conventions.convention: Feature-map transformations are left pullbacks: (L_u f)(x)=f(u⁻¹·x); on group-indexed maps, (L_u F)(g)=F(u⁻¹g). Feature values themselves are unchanged.

Channels are row vectors. The discrete layer uses positive stride, a finite offset set, and unreversed offsets; its unit-stride full-lattice formula is cross-correlation. Padding, cropping and subsampling need not preserve symmetry.
Group correlation uses filter argument g⁻¹h; image-to-group correlation uses g⁻¹·x. Every displayed sum must have finite support or converge absolutely in each output coordinate.

The quarter-turn sends e₁ to e₂, and the reflection sends (x,y) to (x,−y). Pair multiplication is (t,M)(s,N)=(t+Ms,MN). The point groups have four and eight elements; the full p4 and p4m groups are infinite.

Neighborhood pooling uses right offsets gu with finite nonempty U. Coset pooling uses left cosets gH, a finite subgroup H, and the left action a·(gH)=(ag)H. Subgroup restriction preserves the subgroup action.

load_bearing.statement: For a discrete group acting on the left on the square lattice, with every sum finitely supported or absolutely convergent in each output coordinate, group-to-group and image-to-group cross-correlation commute with the induced left actions. Full-lattice unit-stride discrete layers preserve translation equivariance, including fixed origin shifts and constant output bias. Pointwise nonlinearities and finite-neighborhood max pooling without subsampling commute with the left action; subgroup restriction preserves subgroup equivariance; finite-subgroup left-coset pooling is equivariant on G/H and is invariant when H=G is finite. Finite compositions of compatible equivariant layers remain equivariant.
For a group G acting on the left on S and f:S→V, (L_u f)(x)=f(u⁻¹·x) defines a left action on feature maps. For F:G→V, (L_u F)(g)=F(u⁻¹g).
For finite-dimensional row-vector channels, (C_Ψ f)(g)=Σ_h f(h)Ψ(g⁻¹h) and (E_Ψ f)(g)=Σ_x f(x)Ψ(g⁻¹·x), with each sum finitely supported or absolutely convergent in every output coordinate.

Pointwise nonlinearities act componentwise; (P_U F)(g)_c=max_{u∈U}F(gu)_c for finite nonempty U; subgroup sampling is restriction to H; for finite H≤G, (Q_H F)(gH)_c=max_{h∈H}F(gh)_c is well-defined on left cosets with action a·(gH)=(ag)H.

For A=C₄ or D₄, P_A consists of pairs (t,M) with multiplication (t,M)(s,N)=(t+Ms,MN), acting by x↦Mx+t. The point groups have four and eight elements, respectively, while both full lattice groups are infinite.

published_dependencies.used_for: Declared domains, codomains and feature maps as functions.
Associativity, identities and two-sided inverses in pullback actions, lattice groups and correlation reindexing.
Left-action laws and the bijectivity of site transformations.
The intertwining condition between input and output actions and its use in composition.
Identity, multiplication and inverse closure for restriction, coset pooling and the p4 rotation subgroup.
The convention gH={gh:h∈H} and representative-independent coset pooling.

concerns.concern: The final Definition sentence says, “The layer is $G$-invariant when the output action $T'_g$ is the identity on $Y$ for every $g\in G$.” It does not require the layer to satisfy the preceding equivariance equation. Taken as written, this is false: let C₂ swap X={0,1}, let Y={0,1} have trivial action, and let Φ(x)=x. The stated condition holds, but Φ(T_g0)=1≠0=Φ(0). Invariance needs the equation Φ(T_gx)=Φ(x), or an explicit restriction to equivariant layers with trivial output action. The cited Cohen–Welling §2 describes invariance as a special case of equivariance, retaining that requirement: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1602.07576.
